verdictOnCurrentFilms: One template wearing three coats, and none of the coats is the exhibit's. (1) The evidence is a postage stamp: each photograph fills about a quarter of the frame and the rest is a blurred, tinted copy of itself (amber, then grey, then mustard on Douglass; brown gold smears on Persia). That blur is invented signal, a fake bokeh doing the job of a layout, and its colour changes from shot to shot with no logic. (2) Zero typography: no title card, no Anton, no Abril, no Cormorant, no Syriac, no lapis, no signal red. The only type is one default serif in a rounded translucent box, identical in all three films, four or five lines long, overlapping the bottom of the photograph (Ford frame 5, the Persia seal frame where the box sits on the seal). (3) The honesty label is the weakest thing on screen: RECONSTRUCTION and the credit are about 8px grey text in the top right corner, while the painted tea-brown boy and the painted Quadricycle get the biggest, brightest frame. The most important fact in the film is the least visible. (4) The Persia seal sits on a visible black rectangle that does not match the background, a plain compositing defect. (5) Transitions are dissolves and nothing else; frames 2/3 and 5/6 in Douglass and Ford are the same still held, so the film is a slideshow with a voice. (6) The Hartsook portrait of a smiling Ford gets the same weight as the Highland Park line photograph, which flatters the man. What is right: Ford and Douglass real archive photographs are the best things in the frame, the Douglass daguerreotype entrance works, the Persia seal is a genuinely good object. The fix is not more effects. It is a system where the surround carries all the signal and the evidence carries none.
concept: FIDELITY IS PROVENANCE. Every film is a transmission received from the record, and the picture quality tells you what you are looking at. Archive photographs are the clean carrier: locked sync, zero grade, zero noise, pixel-true at rest, always. Everything that is not evidence is signal and is allowed to have a body: the surround, the type, the transitions, the maps. Reconstructions are literally a lower-fidelity transmission: always rendered through a visible 2-3px raster and slightly soft, with a stamped RECONSTRUCTION tag, so the viewer can see what is imagined without reading a label. Each exhibit receives on its own native medium, derived from its design language: Ford is a line-sync that rolls like the assembly belt (vertical hold, time-clock tick); Douglass is an impression, ink spread and plate misregistration (letterpress as analog signal); Persia is a long-distance signal whose echo delay grows with the miles (feedback trail along the road); Partition is two-plate overprint where the colours fail to register, and a line that tears. No glitch preset anywhere: every distortion is generated by a real process in the render (sync offset, ping-pong feedback buffer, channel misregister) driven by the narration's own amplitude, so the surround breathes with the voice. And a hard law: signal effects only live in transitions of 12 frames or fewer and in the surround; distressing material gets none of it.
titleSequence: About 9 seconds, skippable, Enter/Play live from frame one, title set whole (not word by word). 0.0-1.2s black, room tone only. 1.2-3.5s signal acquisition in the exhibit's native medium resolves into ONE untouched archive plate, centred, taking about 55 percent of frame height (never a stamp-sized thumbnail): Ford, a vertical-hold roll settling on the line photograph with a thin red-orange sync bar; Douglass, a black plate being pressed with ink halo spreading 6px outward and gold/brown channels settling from 8px misregister to 0; Persia, one lapis hairline drawn across the dark that then opens like a road to reveal the stele rubbing or seal; Partition, a madder-red plate and a soot plate sliding into register. 3.5-6.5s the title locks in the exhibit's face at 180-240px: 20-frame de-bleed (12px chromatic offset collapsing to 0, the way a CRT locks), then perfectly still. Below it, one line in the system voice: the four-digit years, tabular, which date-tune from 0000 to the first year of the film in 10 frames. 6.5-8.5s epigraph or the narrator's first sentence begins in captions, plate still, hold. Last 12 frames: cut to first scene. End card (6s): a provenance ledger set as a table, e.g. '14 archive photographs . 5 documents . 6 reconstructions (labelled)' with each credit line at 24px, plus the exhibit's colophon and proofing credits for non-Latin text.
typography: Rules: one display face per exhibit, one body serif, one system mono; archive credit and the RECONSTRUCTION tag are never smaller than 24px at 1080p. Display (design-direction faces): Ford, Anton caps, 200-240px titles, 96px chapter heads, tracking -0.01em, #ff4b1f on iron #1a1411; Douglass, Abril Fatface, caps at 200px for titles, sentence case in chapter heads at 110px, #d9b36a on iron-gall #14110d, with the exhibit's handbill slab face for date lines; Persia, Cormorant Garamond bold sentence case, 150-190px, lapis #4f7cff on midnight #0c1020, with real Syriac (Noto Sans Syriac / Serif Syriac) and Chinese stele characters (Noto Serif SC) set at 500-700px, 8-10 percent opacity, behind the title and never overlapping it (the current site's ghost numeral collision is the bug to avoid: reserve a clear zone, the script lives in the empty third of the frame); Partition, Fraunces 700, madder #e8553d on soot #120f0c, title stacked in English plus Urdu (Noto Nastaliq Urdu), Hindi (Noto Sans Devanagari), Punjabi (Gurmukhi and Shahmukhi), each at a different registration offset, English locks first. Body and captions: Source Serif 4 semibold 46px at 1080p, never Georgia. System voice: IBM Plex Mono 24-26px, tracked 0.06em, tabular figures. Treatment: type is flat, crisp, ungraded; the signal body is in its motion (de-bleed on arrival, 1-2px sync wobble driven by voice amplitude on display type only, never on captions, which must stay perfectly readable).
captionsAndLowerThirds: Kill the translucent rounded box. Captions: Source Serif 4 semibold 46px (36px floor for the 720p cut), left-aligned to a fixed 12-column grid, max 2 lines of about 42 characters, set on the bottom 14 percent of the frame on a solid near-black strip with a 2px exhibit-colour hairline above it, so they never overlap the photograph; photographs are letterboxed up above the strip. The current 4-5 line paragraphs are split into 2-line cues timed to word alignment; the currently spoken word is full opacity, unspoken words 55 percent, no bouncing, no per-word scale. Provenance slip (lower-third replacement): bottom-left above the caption strip, appears 12 frames after the image locks and holds the whole shot. Two kinds only. ARCHIVE: a solid black tag, white mono caps, then institution, date, licence at 24px. RECONSTRUCTION: a hollow 3px #ff6b57 stamped box, mono bold caps 30px, 5 degree-free (no tilt), slams in on the entry transition frame with a thunk, then one line under it: 'imagined from [named sources]; no photograph survives'. The raster on a reconstruction stays on for the whole hold. Names and places on screen use the system mono in exhibit colour with a 4px underline that draws left to right in 8 frames. Chapter slates for new years: the date-tune counter at 96px, 30 frames, over a held still.
transitions: 1. LOCK (default archive-to-archive): outgoing frame slips 3 percent horizontally over 4 frames with a 2px tear line, incoming snaps locked on frame 5; 8 frames total, lands on the narrator's breath, never mid-word. Archive is never distorted at rest. 2. HOLD-ROLL (Ford chapter changes, factory scenes): incoming rolls up from the bottom like a vertical-hold slip over 14 frames with a 40px black sync bar, 2-frame overshoot, audio: single clock tick at frame 1. 3. IMPRESSION (Douglass between two plates): next plate pressed down, scale 1.012 to 1 over 10 frames, ink halo spreading 6px outward, gold and brown channels misregistered 8px settling to 0, the old plate dims 40 percent underneath for 6 frames. 4. THREAD (Persia place-to-place): a lapis hairline draws across at the pace of the sentence (18-30 frames) and the next image wipes in behind it with a 40px soft edge; the line leaves a feedback echo whose delay grows from 6 to 30 frames as the film travels east, so distance is felt as lag. 5. BORDER-TEAR (Partition, used once or twice only, for the line being drawn): the frame splits along a jagged line, halves drift 3 percent apart over 20 frames in two inks, then hold; never used on a human-face photograph or on violence. 6. TRACKING-ERROR ENTRY (any archive-to-Reconstruction cut, all four films): a 6-frame tracking band travels top to bottom, the 3px raster fades in to 35 percent, RECONSTRUCTION stamp lands; the return to archive is the opposite and the cleanest cut in the film: a 2-frame hard snap to full-fidelity, no flash, which reads as 'back to the record'. 7. DATE-TUNE (every film, each time the year jumps): four digits scramble 10 frames and lock left to right, 6 frames apart, over a held still. 8. BREATH-CUT (gated or distressing material, and the very last scene): hard cut to black for 24 frames then hard cut in, no effect, room tone dropped to silence; this is the only transition allowed near enslavement, the Dearborn Independent and Partition violence.
motionGraphics: Ford: the signature graphic is the 12.5 hours to 93 minutes comparison on a belt: two Anton figures in #ff4b1f ('750 MIN' counting down to '93 MIN') while a row of chassis outlines moves along a belt that speeds up with the count; build on the site's own .line component (belt, chassis svg, readout). Then 15 million Model T as a counter that ticks like a time clock for 90 frames, with the correct dates. Douglass: kinetic composing stick: the 1845 title page line 'WRITTEN BY HIMSELF' is set sort by sort into a stick in Abril Fatface gold, each letter dropping with a small clack in sequence, then the stick slides out and the real title page photograph replaces it. Persia: a lapis route map drawn on midnight from Edessa and Seleucia-Ctesiphon to Chang'an, dated waypoints (410, 635, 781), the line carrying the growing echo, the real Syriac and Chinese stele script set big and faded behind; waypoints are mono labels with underline-draw. Partition: the Radcliffe line drawn as a trace over the outline map (reuse public/dossier/partition-map.html geometry) at the speed of the sentence, two inks failing to register by 6px, then names of places in Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi, English snapping to lock in that order; the 'line' number cards are plain figures, no bar-race gaiety. All charts: flat colour, numbers tabular, a source line on screen for any figure, and under 4 seconds each.

perExhibit.douglass: Abril Fatface gold on iron-gall. Native medium: letterpress impression. Archive plates enlarged to 55-60 percent of frame height with the daguerreotype oval kept on its gold mat as scanned; the blurred amber background is deleted and replaced with flat iron-gall brown-black and a faint paper-fibre noise on the SURROUND only. Transition IMPRESSION between plates, composing-stick kinetic type for the 1845 title page. The boy-chalking-a-plank faceless Reconstruction gets the raster and the stamp; do not use the confident painted faces (lectern, study) at all. Enslavement material uses BREATH-CUT only, gated, silent, no gold type shimmer.
perExhibit.ford: Anton in signal red-orange on iron. Native medium: line-sync and time-clock. Keep the real Highland Park line photograph largest and longest-held; the smiling Hartsook portrait is demoted to a short held plate or cut, with Ford otherwise back-turned (the Quadricycle painting already is). B-24 painting stays, labelled and rastered. HOLD-ROLL at chapter changes, the 750-to-93 minute belt graphic, parts-bin stencil numerals for dates. The Beliefs and Morals chapter is plain: same type, same size, no sync bar, no roll, BREATH-CUT in and out, real Dearborn Independent pages as archive plates; the signal bender's one concession is silence, not style.
perExhibit.persia: Cormorant Garamond in lapis on midnight, real Syriac and Chinese script large and faded in the empty third of the frame, proofed by named native readers. Native medium: long-distance signal with growing echo. THREAD transitions along a route map, the Syriac gospel and Ctesiphon vault Reconstructions keep their raster and stamp, the British Museum seal composited properly on its own matched ground (kill the black rectangle) and left ungraded. No gold: lapis only, so it is not Douglass.
perExhibit.partition: Fraunces in madder red on soot. Native medium: two-plate overprint that fails to register, and the map line. Title in Urdu, Hindi, Punjabi, English at four registration offsets, English locking first. BORDER-TEAR used once, on the line being drawn, never on a person. All violence and displacement-march photographs are gated, silent, BREATH-CUT, no motion on the plate. Real photographs and testimony primary; no Reconstruction faces.

soundTies: Narration is the master clock. Run forced alignment (Whisper word timestamps or the TTS alignment JSON) once per film; captions, transition frames, and slips all read from that JSON, so every cut lands on a breath or a consonant, never mid-word. Narrator amplitude (RMS envelope at 30fps) drives the surround: sync-wobble on display type, line thickness of the Persia thread and the Ford sync bar, ink halo size on Douglass, so the graphics literally breathe with the voice (it is real feedback, not a preset). Per-transition foley: Ford clock tick and belt hum bed (a low 55Hz line hum at -34 dB), Douglass wood-and-metal clack on each sort and a press thunk on IMPRESSION, Persia a single soft bowed-string swell tail whose length equals the echo delay, Partition a dry paper tear. RECONSTRUCTION stamp gets its own thunk, always identical, so the ear learns the label. Score: one sustained bed per film, ducked 8 dB under VO, mix -18 LUFS; the score drops out entirely (not fades) at BREATH-CUT moments. Captions are the accessible mirror: no information carried by sound alone.
productionMethod: Playwright renders deterministic HTML/CSS/WebGL frames at 1920x1080, 30fps, driven by a pure time function t(frame) so any frame is reproducible; ffmpeg encodes H.264 CRF 16, 8-bit, with the VO and score muxed. Type, captions, provenance slips, chapter slates: HTML/CSS with real fonts (Anton, Abril Fatface, Cormorant Garamond, Fraunces, Noto Syriac/SC/Nastaliq/Devanagari/Gurmukhi, Source Serif 4, IBM Plex Mono). Signal effects (hold-roll, tear, tracking band, channel misregister, feedback trail via ping-pong framebuffers, raster on reconstructions): small WebGL fragment shaders in the same page; archive photographs are uploaded as untouched textures drawn 1:1 (point-sampled to the exact crop) and bypass every shader at rest. Maps and routes: SVG paths animated by stroke-dashoffset, reusing public/dossier/partition-map.html geometry. Small repeat motifs (stamp slam, date-tune digits, composing-stick sorts, end-card ledger rows): Lottie/dotLottie authored once, shared. Pillow: contact sheets for QA, pre-scaling and mat/background compositing (fix the seal rectangle), provenance end-card rasters. Magnific: not needed for motion; use zero credits on effects, and do not use it to make faces; at most re-run labelled Reconstruction paintings without faces. Fabula and Tela: only as the owner's editable assembly of the final captions and cue list. Verification gate: decode a locked frame, crop every ARCHIVE plate region, and fail the build if PSNR against the source scaled crop is under 40dB (proves the evidence is ungraded); automated check that every Reconstruction frame carries the raster and the stamp; frame-by-frame luminance flash check under 3 flashes per second.
risk: Signal effects read as a gimmick or as a trendy glitch pass, and critics will say it is grading the evidence. Mitigation is the discipline above: effects only in the surround and in transitions of 14 frames or fewer, photographs pixel-true at rest, and the PSNR gate to prove it. Other risks: raster and scanlines moire or band badly after H.264 on phones (use a 3px period at 1080p, test on a real phone and TV, ship a no-raster fallback that uses a hollow frame border instead); rolling and tearing can trigger photosensitive discomfort (no strobe, no full-frame flashes, cap luminance delta, reduced-motion cut with a 150ms fade); and the whole-family concept can look cold if the surround is too clean, so the exhibit colour and the type must carry warmth. Finally, the Ford Beliefs chapter and Partition violence must stay effect-free; if the film feels stylistically dead there that is correct.

arguesWith.why: CINEMATIC will want to unify the family with a lens language: halation, film grain, a 2.39 letterbox, a graded lift on the archive and a slow push on every still. That is imperfection faked in post, and on evidence it is the same violet-sepia filter the council just retired, only more expensive. Grain you add is a lie about where the picture came from; the scan's real grain, dust and plate edge are the only texture the photograph is allowed to carry. I will give CINEMATIC the held shot, the silence before the hard chapter and a 2 percent slow push on Reconstructions only, never on photographs, but a grade on archive is a line I will not cross.
